economics.externalities-analyse-1.0003.all: Plan: ban cuts negative externality of consumption (litter, harm to wildlife, cleanup costs); cleaner beaches/rivers raise tourism and fishing incomes, lower clean-up spending; moves output toward socially optimal level; limited by illegal use and enforcement cost.

economics.externalities-analyse-2.0004.all: Plan: negative externality of production; third parties (fishermen) lose income from reduced fish stocks; social cost > private cost so overproduction; possible health/environment costs; market failure, firm ignores external cost.

economics.externalities-analyse-3.0006.all: Plan: vaccinated people reduce spread to third parties (herd immunity, rate 61->88%); fewer sick days so higher productivity; lower healthcare costs for government; social benefit > private benefit so underconsumed without subsidy.

economics.externalities-assess-1.0006.all: Plan: ban effective (cleaner beaches/rivers), simple, certain; but illegal use, costly enforcement, substitutes may also pollute, no revenue; compare with tax; conclusion depends on enforcement.

economics.externalities-assess-2.0001.all: Plan: tax internalises external cost, raises revenue, incentive to cut pollution; but hard to value external cost, may cut output/jobs (1351 workers), inelastic demand; alternatives regulation/permits; judgement.

economics.externalities-assess-3.0002.all: Plan: positive externalities, higher uptake 63->85%, lower health costs; but opportunity cost, may have happened anyway, cost per extra child; judgement.

economics.externalities-data.0016.b: Plan: herd immunity protects non-vaccinated third parties; fewer sick days, higher productivity; lower healthcare costs; 64->87% uptake.
economics.externalities-data.0016.c: Plan: for - positive externalities, underconsumption corrected, equity; against - opportunity cost, tax burden, information failure better addressed by education; judgement depends on cost vs benefits.

economics.externalities-define1.0002.all: A cost to a third party not involved in the production or consumption of a good (social cost > private cost)

economics.externalities-define2.0001.all: A cost or benefit (spillover) affecting third parties not involved in the transaction, not reflected in price

economics.externalities-describe.0002.all: Vaccination creates positive externalities (protects others from infection) so it is underconsumed in free market; subsidy lowers price, raises consumption to social optimum

economics.externalities-evaluate-2.0003.all: Plan: tax internalises cost, polluter pays, revenue; but valuation difficulty, job losses (2338), inelastic demand, firm relocation; alternatives regulation, permits; conclusion.

economics.externalities-evaluate-3.0006.all: Plan: herd immunity, 72->94%, lower healthcare cost, productivity; opportunity cost, inefficiency, some would vaccinate anyway; conclusion.

economics.fiscal-analyse-2.0004.all: Plan: green jobs cut unemployment, multiplier; investment boosts growth/productivity; lower pollution externalities; export opportunities, energy security.

economics.fiscal-analyse-3.0001.all: Plan: indirect taxes don't directly reduce reward for work; broad base, hard to evade; can target demerit goods; quick to change; raise revenue for healthcare.

economics.fiscal-assess-1.0005.all: Plan: deficit 6.7% and debt 89% high - interest costs, confidence; but cuts reduce AD, growth, unemployment, regressive sales tax; timing matters; judgement.
